subject: HC triage: seat-swap vs. replacement request (freeze exception)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Seat-swap triage: senior eng notice — options and ask

Hi Evelyn / Karthik,

Quick recap: Marco from Aperture informed us yesterday that their lead infra engineer (Nadia Patel) has accepted another offer and will be off in 6 weeks. That role was tied directly to the integration work our Dedicated infra team is owning for that account.

Options I see (tradeoffs below):
- Request freeze exception to backfill one full-time Senior FE (recommended by product to keep SLA and roadmap intact).
- Do an internal seat-swap: move a growth infra seat from Growth Eng team (open but prioritized lower) and reassign two contractors for 12 weeks to cover critical delivery.
- Delay scope and renegotiate timeline with Aperture (risk: churn/discount request).

Asks:
1) Approval to submit a formal freeze-exception for a replacement hire (I will attach JD + impact matrix).
2) If we do not get approval, permission to start seat-swap planning and formalize contractor extension (contract dollars TBD).

I've attached an initial impact matrix and the draft JD. High-level cost delta is in the matrix; replacement FTE cost ~ $220k OTE, contractor cover ~ $85k/quarter.

Pointing Ben in — he can share budget runway numbers for Q3.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Dedicated Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Tara Holt <tara.holt@peopleops.example.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seat-swap triage: senior eng notice — options and ask

Thanks for the summary, Laura.

A couple quick clarifying questions before I escalate to People Ops for a formal exception:
- Which deliverables (by milestone) will be at risk if we do not backfill? Please add specific dates and owner swaps if we do seat-swap.
- Can Ben confirm whether we have any hiring buffer in the Q3 reserved headcount pool or if we need to reallocate from other teams?

Operationally I am open to a temporary exception if we get a 90-day review checkpoint and a plan to avoid compounding the HC deficit elsewhere. Tara — looping you in so People Ops can flag what paperwork we need for an exception and the expected approval SLAs.

If you can get me the milestones + Ben's runway note by EOD Monday I will decide whether to escalate to the SVP for a sign-off.

Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product & Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Tara Holt <tara.holt@peopleops.example.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seat-swap triage: senior eng notice — options and ask

Adding the numbers and scenarios we modeled (attached as impact-matrix.xlsx and hc-scenarios.pdf). Short summary:

Scenario A — Replace (freeze exception):
- Time to hire (target fill): 8–10 weeks from req approval
- Cost delta (hire comp + hiring costs): ~ $220k runrate annualized, immediate budget hit absorbed by Q3 hiring pool if we reallocate 0.4F from X-team.
- Risk: none to roadmap; long-term HC count unchanged.

Scenario B — Seat-swap + contractor bridge:
- Time to implement: 3 weeks to reassign, contractors onboarded in 2 weeks
- Cost delta: contractors ~ $85k/quarter + internal productivity rampdown cost (~5–10% across the donor team).
- Risk: donor team's OKR delivery reduced; 30% chance of missed milestone for feature Y (client-facing).

Recommendation: Approve a 90-day temporary freeze exception to post a replacement req today. We should also run a parallel seat-swap contingency plan to reduce delivery risk during the hiring window.

Ben — confirmed there is a small Q3 buffer but we would need to reprioritize one smaller hire in Infra Tools if we take on a replacement now.

Tara — if you can confirm the People Ops checklist for a temporary exception (forms, approvals required, expected timeline), we'll kick this off today.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Tara Holt <tara.holt@peopleops.example.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seat-swap triage: senior eng notice — options and ask

OK — approved (temporary freeze exception). Conditions:
1) This is a 90-day exception window starting today (2026-05-12). We post the req immediately and target a 60–75 day fill.
2) Laura to run the seat-swap contingency plan in parallel (transfer plan + contractor taper) and share a weekly status (Mon updates) for the first 8 weeks.
3) Hiring must not increase net HC beyond the current Q3 plan without explicit SVP approval; we reallocate the Infra Tools headcount as discussed.
4) Tara — please initiate the exception workflow, confirm required sign-offs (HR legal + finance) and set expectation for final SVP sign-off if needed.

Laura — once People Ops confirms, go ahead and publish the JD and start speaking with two priority candidates we have in the pipe. Communicate the role's shipping-critical scope clearly so we avoid mismatches.

Thanks all — keeping Aperture in the loop: Marco, we'll need to provide a short contingency communication to manage expectations (Laura will draft).

Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product & Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
